full_text_en:
Agricultural Bank of China Limited, Jilin Dongsheng Branch v. Jilin Bibixi Foreign Language Experimental School — dispute over loan guarantee contract (enforcement case)

【Ruling Summary】

1. Exemption from enforcement must be expressly provided for by laws or regulations. Current laws and regulations do not provide for exemption from enforcement of educational land or educational facilities. A school shall bear its debts with its property, including educational land and educational facilities.

2. A balance shall be maintained between the realization of creditor's rights and the protection of social public interests. Enforcement measures taken by the court shall not affect the use of social public welfare facilities. To safeguard the development of social public welfare undertakings and protect the basic rights and interests of the public, such as the right to education, the enforcement of educational land and educational facilities shall not change their public welfare use and shall not affect their actual use.

Enforcement Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2015) Zhi Shen Zi No. 55

Complainant (Enforcement Applicant): Agricultural Bank of China Limited, Jilin Dongsheng Branch. Address: No. 201, Jilin Street, Jilin City, Jilin Province.

Responsible Person: Sui Yang, Branch President.

Agent ad litem: Song Junfeng, Employee of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Guo Zhihui, Employee of the Company.

Respondent (Enforcement Respondent): Jilin Bibixi Foreign Language Experimental School. Address: No. 2, Lianhua Hutong, Changyi District, Jilin City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Feng, Principal of the School.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Shujie, Employee of the School.

Agent ad litem: Li Xiaoli, Employee of the School.

Enforcement Respondent: Jilin Bibixi Economic and Trade Information Consulting Co., Ltd. Address: No. 2, Lianhua Street, Changyi District, Jilin City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Feng, Chairman of the Company.

Agricultural Bank of China Limited, Jilin Dongsheng Branch (hereinafter referred to as the ABC Dongsheng Branch), in connection with the enforcement case of a dispute over a loan guarantee contract with Jilin Bibixi Foreign Language Experimental School (hereinafter referred to as the Bibixi School), dissatisfied with the Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhi Fu Zi No. 29 of the Jilin High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the Jilin High Court), filed a complaint with this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Zhao Jinshan, Acting Judge Pan Yongfeng, and Acting Judge Ge Hongtao to conduct the review, with Clerk Liu Wei recording. This case has now been concluded upon review.

The Jilin High Court found the following: In the enforcement case of a dispute over a loan guarantee contract between the ABC Dongsheng Branch and the enforcement respondents, the Bibixi School and Jilin Bibixi Economic and Trade Information Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Bibixi Consulting Company), based on the Civil Judgment (2006) Ji Zhong Min Er Chu Zi No. 101 of the Jilin Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the Jilin Intermediate Court), the defendant Bibixi School was ordered to repay the plaintiff ABC Dongsheng Branch two loans totaling RMB 6,760,000 in principal, and pay interest totaling RMB 87,398.82; if the defendant Bibixi School failed to repay one of the loans of RMB 5,880,000 in principal and related interest on time, the plaintiff ABC Dongsheng Branch would have priority in receiving compensation from the proceeds of the sale of the collateral under the maximum amount mortgage contract, i.e., the office building owned by the defendant Bibixi Consulting Company. After the ABC Dongsheng Branch appealed, the Jilin High Court rendered Civil Judgment (2006) Ji Min San Zhong Zi No. 227, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

After the judgment became effective, the Bibixi School and the Bibixi Consulting Company failed to fulfill the legal obligations determined by the judgment on time. The ABC Dongsheng Branch applied for enforcement on April 7, 2009, and the Jilin Intermediate Court opened a case on the same day. During enforcement, the Jilin Intermediate Court lawfully appraised and auctioned the mortgaged office building of the Bibixi Consulting Company. After three auctions, the property was not sold due to no registrations, and the floor price was RMB 6,463,385.60. After a private sale by the Jilin Intermediate Court, the proceeds were RMB 6,307,723.60, which were delivered to the ABC Dongsheng Branch. On August 31, 2010, the ABC Dongsheng Branch submitted a written application to the Jilin Intermediate Court requesting termination of enforcement and retention of the creditor's rights. On August 31, 2010, the Jilin Intermediate Court issued Enforcement Ruling (2007) Ji Zhong Min Zhi Zi No. 125, ruling that the civil judgment (2006) Ji Zhong Min Er Chu Zi No. 101 be terminated with the creditor's rights retained. Later, the ABC Dongsheng Branch applied to resume enforcement. The Jilin Intermediate Court resumed enforcement on March 4, 2014, and issued Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Hui Zi No. 20 on March 11 of the same year, sealing the land use right located at No. 14, Lianhe Street, Lianhua Street, Changyi District, Jilin City, with an area of 4,314.68 square meters and land use right certificate No. Ji Guo Yong (2003) Di XXXXXXXXXX6, and the building ownership located at No. 14, Lianhe Street, Lianhua Street, Changyi District, Jilin City, with a building area of 1,556.06 square meters and building ownership certificate No. Jilin Shi Fang Quan Zheng Chang Zi QTXXXXXXXX4, for a period of two years from March 11, 2014 to March 10, 2016.

The Bibixi School filed an objection with the Jilin Intermediate Court, arguing that it is a social public welfare organization engaged in education, and the sealed land and buildings are educational land and educational facilities currently in use. The court's sealing and further enforcement measures would inevitably seriously affect the normal educational work of the Bibixi School and affect the learning of students currently enrolled. Therefore, it requested the court to lift the sealing of the above land use right and buildings, or to postpone further enforcement measures. It requested the revocation of Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Hui Zi No. 20 and the lifting of the sealing.

After review, the Jilin Intermediate Court held that although the sealed land and buildings were educational land and educational facilities, the Bibixi School had not met the conditions for running a school, as the buildings and land were idle, and its non-enterprise legal person business term had expired, making it unqualified to run a school. Therefore, the objection could not be sustained and should be rejected. On June 26, 2014, the Jilin Intermediate Court issued Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Xing Yi Zi No. 16, dismissing the objection of the Bibixi School in accordance with Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law).

Dissatisfied with the above ruling of the Jilin Intermediate Court, the Bibixi School applied for reconsideration to the Jilin High Court, arguing that as a social public welfare organization engaged in education, the land use right and buildings sealed by the Jilin Intermediate Court were educational buildings and land in use, and the sealing and further enforcement measures would inevitably seriously affect normal educational work. The infrastructure construction around the school had basically ended, and the school had applied to the education authority to resume enrollment, and the conditions for running the school would be further improved. It requested the revocation of Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Hui Zi No. 20 and Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Xing Yi Zi No. 16, and the lifting of the sealing.

The Jilin High Court additionally found that the disputed building was originally the school's laboratory building, and the property right certificate indicated that the design use was medical; the land use right certificate recorded the use as educational land, with the acquisition method being allocated land. The legal person registration of the Bibixi School indicated that its nature was a private non-enterprise legal person, with a business scope of a private school integrating preschool, primary, and junior high education, a social schooling institution mainly providing educational services. The Bibixi School used this building and land as collateral for a loan from the ABC Dongsheng Branch, which was ruled invalid by the Jilin Intermediate Court and the Jilin High Court. Regarding the Bibixi School's qualification to run a school, the Jilin Municipal Education Bureau replied in a letter stating that "In 2011, due to infrastructure construction around the school, it could not enroll students and applied to suspend enrollment. On April 28, 2014, the school applied to resume enrollment. Upon review and approval by our bureau, it may be allowed to continue running the school."

The Jilin High Court held that the superior authority, the Jilin Municipal Education Bureau, clearly stated in its reply letter that the school could continue running and resume enrollment. As a public welfare institution, the Bibixi School mortgaged its land use right and building ownership to a bank for a loan, which was ruled invalid by the Jilin High Court's civil judgment. Therefore, the people's court could not enforce the above property. The Jilin Intermediate Court's Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Xing Yi Zi No. 16 lacked legal basis. After discussion by the Civil and Commercial Adjudication Professional Committee of the Jilin High Court at its 19th meeting, in accordance with Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law and Articles 8 and 9 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China in Enforcement Proceedings, on December 4, 2014, it issued Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhi Fu Zi No. 29, revoking the Jilin Intermediate Court's Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Hui Zi No. 20 and Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Xing Yi Zi No. 16.

Dissatisfied with the above ruling of the Jilin High Court, the ABC Dongsheng Branch appealed to this Court, requesting the revocation of the Jilin High Court's Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhi Fu Zi No. 29. Its main reasons were as follows: First, the facts found and the law applied in the ruling were erroneous. Although the mortgage handled by the Bibixi School at the time of the loan was ruled invalid by the court, this should not affect the ABC Dongsheng Branch's right to demand that the Bibixi School repay the debts owed with its own property, including the building and land. The property of the Bibixi School does not fall within the category of property that the people's court may not seal, freeze, or seize as listed in Article 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Sealing, Freezing, and Seizing Property in Civil Enforcement by the People's Courts. Second, the Bibixi School is a private non-enterprise legal person established with capital from Chen Feng, and its business term had expired, and its business qualification had not been renewed for many years. Since 2010, the school had had no students, the teaching building had been auctioned by the court, the teacher's office building was abandoned, and the school playground had become a driving school practice area. Although the existing buildings and land were educational land and facilities, they were idle. The school existed in name only and should not be recognized as a public welfare institution. Third, the non-performing assets in this case had been stripped to the Ministry of Finance, and it was hoped that the safety of state-owned assets would be effectively protected.

After cross-examination, the ABC Dongsheng Branch supplemented its opinion as follows: First, according to the currently effective Interim Regulations on the Registration and Administration of Private Non-Enterprise Units, civil affairs departments at all levels are the registration authorities for private schools, and private schools need to obtain a registration certificate for private non-enterprise units to be established and operate. Education departments are only the business supervisory authorities. Second, the Bibixi School's private non-enterprise unit registration certificate was revoked by the Jilin Municipal Civil Affairs Bureau on April 29, 2011. Therefore, the legal person status of the Bibixi School no longer exists, and it is no longer a public welfare institution. There is nothing improper about the court enforcing its own property to repay its own debts. Even if the Bibixi School were still a public welfare institution, the Jilin Intermediate Court's enforcement ruling sealing its own assets complies with the law. The Bibixi School's argument for lifting the sealing and suspending enforcement on the grounds that it is applying to resume running the school has no legal basis. Third, after the ABC Dongsheng Branch applied to resume enforcement and the sealing was made, the Bibixi School applied to the Jilin Municipal Education Bureau to resume enrollment, intending to prevent further enforcement by the court, with the fundamental purpose of evading bank debts.

In its cross-examination, the Bibixi School stated in its defense that the Jilin High Court's 2006 judgment had ruled that the mortgage on the disputed subject matter was invalid. The disputed subject matter was educational land and educational buildings used by the Bibixi School for public welfare purposes and should not be enforced. The Bibixi School had already repaid more than RMB 6 million of the principal to the creditor, leaving only a small portion of principal and interest unpaid. The ABC Dongsheng Branch had repeatedly requested the Jilin Municipal Education Bureau to cancel the Bibixi School's qualification to run a school, but the Jilin Municipal Education Bureau replied three times that the Bibixi School had the qualification to run a school and could continue. Now the civil affairs department no longer has the authority to manage schools, and the Bibixi School only needs to register with the civil affairs department after resuming operations. The Jilin High Court's reconsideration ruling should be upheld.

The Bibixi Consulting Company did not provide a defense.

Upon review, in addition to confirming the facts found by the Jilin High Court, this Court found the following: The "Jiangcheng Evening News" on April 30, 2011, published an announcement of the Jilin Municipal Civil Affairs Bureau's administrative penalty decision (No. 5), which stated: "The following 77 private non-enterprise units have not participated in annual inspections and have been unable to carry out normal activities for many years. According to the provisions of the Interim Regulations on the Registration and Administration of Private Non-Enterprise Units, they are decided to be deregistered. From this date, their certificates and official seals are abolished (April 14, 2011)." The list of deregistered units included "Jilin Bibixi Foreign Language Experimental School."

In response to the Agricultural Bank of China Jilin Branch, the Jilin Municipal Education Bureau issued a letter titled "Reply on the Qualification of Jilin Bibixi Foreign Language Experimental School to Run a School" (Ji Shi Jiao Han [2015] No. 24) on June 5, 2015, which stated: "1. Regarding the qualification to run a school. Jilin Bibixi Foreign Language Experimental School was approved for trial operation by our bureau in 1995 and formally established in 1998. In 2011, due to infrastructure construction around the school, the school requested to suspend enrollment, with the qualification to run a school legally retained. 2. Regarding the resumption of enrollment. Because the property certificate of the school dormitory building is pledged with your bank's Dongsheng Branch, the school cannot improve its conditions, and our bureau cannot currently legally evaluate it. 3. Regarding the matter raised by your bank in accordance with Articles 9, 62, and 8 of Chapter 9 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion of Private Education, since the school suspended enrollment, it has not been able to carry out normal educational and teaching activities and has had no capital flows, so we also cannot evaluate it."

This Court holds that, based on the complaint of the complainant and the defense of the respondent, the focus of the dispute in this case is the issue of the Bibixi School's legal personality and whether the educational land and educational facilities of the Bibixi School can be exempted from enforcement.

First, regarding the issue of the Bibixi School's legal personality. Prior to the resumption of enforcement in this case, the Bibixi School was publicly deregistered as a private non-enterprise (legal person) unit by the Jilin Municipal Civil Affairs Bureau. According to Article 27 of the Interim Regulations on the Registration and Administration of Private Non-Enterprise Units, "If a unit engages in activities under the name of a private non-enterprise unit without registration, or continues to engage in activities under the name of a private non-enterprise unit after being deregistered, the registration authority shall ban it and confiscate illegal property; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be pursued according to law; if a crime is not constituted, public security penalties shall be imposed according to law." The Bibixi School could not continue to engage in activities in the name of the Bibixi School. However, the Bibixi School had not yet completed the cancellation of registration. According to Article 16, Paragraph 2 of the Interim Regulations on the Registration and Administration of Private Non-Enterprise Units, "Before a private non-enterprise unit completes the cancellation of registration, it shall, under the guidance of the competent business unit and other relevant authorities, establish a liquidation organization and complete the liquidation work. During the liquidation period, the private non-enterprise unit shall not engage in activities other than liquidation." Therefore, after being deregistered and before completing the cancellation of registration, the legal personality of the Bibixi School still existed, but its capacity for rights and conduct was limited, and it could only engage in activities within the scope of liquidation. The Bibixi School's participation in enforcement proceedings as an enforcement respondent was part of the work of settling its creditor's rights and debts. If the Bibixi School had not established a liquidation organization in accordance with the law and was not allowed to participate in enforcement proceedings in the name of the unit, it would be impossible to carry out the corresponding work of settling creditor's rights and debts. By reference to Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (II), which provides that "Before a company completes liquidation and cancellation of registration, civil lawsuits concerning the company shall be conducted in the name of the company. If the company has established a liquidation organization, the head of the liquidation organization shall represent the company in litigation; if no liquidation organization has been established, the original legal representative shall represent the company in litigation," the Bibixi School could participate in enforcement proceedings in the name of the unit to settle its creditor's rights and debts before cancellation of registration. In this case, the Bibixi School's activities in the name of the unit must be strictly limited to the necessary activities in participating in enforcement proceedings and must not engage in activities beyond the settlement of existing creditor's rights and debts. The Bibixi School is a private school. According to Article 3, Paragraph 1 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Promotion of Private Education (hereinafter referred to as the Private Education Promotion Law), "Private education is a public welfare undertaking and is a component of the socialist education undertaking." Therefore, the ABC Dongsheng Branch's assertion that the Bibixi School's legal personality no longer exists and that it is no longer a public welfare institution lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

Second, regarding the issue of whether educational facilities and educational land may be exempt from execution. The land and real estate in dispute in this case are educational land and educational facilities of a public interest nature. Bibixi School had previously used the above ownership of the houses and land use rights to create a mortgage in favor of Agricultural Bank of China, Dongsheng Sub-branch, which was ruled invalid by the court on the ground that it violated mandatory provisions of the law. Although the law explicitly prohibits schools from using educational facilities to create mortgages, there are currently no restrictive or prohibitive provisions in laws or administrative regulations regarding the compulsory enforcement of educational land or educational facilities. The Law on the Promotion of Private Education provides for the termination and liquidation obligations of private schools and specifies the order of debt repayment. During the liquidation of a private school, it is inherent that the school's property, including educational land and educational facilities, should be sold to satisfy the debts owed by the school. However, based on considerations of public interest, educational land and educational facilities do have special characteristics different from ordinary property. This special nature is manifested in the specific use of educational facilities. For a school to accomplish its educational and teaching objectives and achieve the social public interest goal of educating people, it requires various educational and teaching facilities. If compulsory enforcement is carried out on educational facilities that the school is currently using, it would not only affect the normal order of education and teaching, but improper handling could also cause students to lose access to schooling, thereby harming the public's right to education. Therefore, although there is no clear provision in China's laws and administrative regulations on whether educational facilities may be exempt from execution, in order to safeguard the development of public interest undertakings and protect basic rights such as the public's right to education, the enforcement of educational land and educational facilities must not change their original public interest use, nor affect their actual use. In this case, although Bibixi School currently has no enrolled students and the disputed educational land and educational facilities are all idle, with no direct and actual harm to the right to education of enrolled students, Bibixi School's school-running license has not been revoked. The reply letter from Jilin Municipal Bureau of Education indicates that Bibixi School still retains its school-running qualifications and there is a possibility of resuming enrollment. In order to fully protect the public interest, the execution of the disputed educational land and educational facilities in this case must also be premised on not affecting the performance of their educational functions. At the same time, the fundamental purpose of the compulsory enforcement procedure is to realize the creditor's rights confirmed by effective legal instruments. As long as it does not affect the normal use of educational land and educational facilities, the people's court should take necessary enforcement measures based on the application of the enforcement applicant to protect the lawful rights and interests of the enforcement applicant. Since laws and regulations do not prohibit the transfer of educational land and educational facilities, where there is a possibility of transfer, sealing-up should be permitted on the premise that it does not affect use. Given that the content of Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Hui Zi No. 20 of Jilin Intermediate People's Court is merely to seal up the disputed land and real estate in this case, and sealing up can be carried out on the premise that it does not affect normal use, the claim of Agricultural Bank of China, Dongsheng Sub-branch that the sealing up of Bibixi School's own assets by Jilin Intermediate People's Court complies with legal provisions should be supported. Although Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Xing Yi Zi No. 16 of Jilin Intermediate People's Court did not explicitly point out that enforcement measures must be taken on the disputed land and real estate in this case on the premise of not affecting their normal use, that ruling maintained the sealing up of the disputed property, and there was no error in its result. Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhi Fu Zi No. 29 of Jilin High People's Court directly revoked the above enforcement rulings without legal basis and should be corrected.

In summary, in accordance with Article 154 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 129 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement Work of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation), the ruling is as follows:

Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhi Fu Zi No. 29 of Jilin High People's Court is revoked, and Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Xing Yi Zi No. 16 and Enforcement Ruling (2014) Ji Zhong Zhi Hui Zi No. 20 of Jilin Intermediate People's Court of Jilin City, Jilin Province are affirmed.

This ruling shall take effect immediately upon service.

Presiding Judge: Zhao Jinshan

Acting Judge: Pan Yongfeng

Acting Judge: Ge Hongtao

August 5, 2015

Clerk: Liu Wei

About the Presiding Judge

Senior Judge Zhao Jinshan, born in 1970, holds a Doctor of Laws degree, and has served as a judge of the Supreme People's Court since 2010.
